maps.heading: Getting into the map box on Google
paragraphs: We reviewed 54 Google results pages across the six GCC countries in November 2026. Every “web design company” search we checked for Dubai, Riyadh and Doha showed a map box of three local businesses above the regular results. Your customers’ searches for “clinic in Riyadh” or “restaurant in Dubai” work in a similar way.

rules.heading: Selling online in Saudi Arabia and the UAE
rules.lead: Each market has rules a store has to meet. We set your store up with the pages and price display they call for: your business details, delivery and returns, and prices shown with VAT. The licence and tax registration stay with you.

markets.title: Saudi Arabia
points: The E-Commerce Law (Royal Decree M/126, 2019) requires your store to show who you are and how to reach you, and to show the total price including taxes and fees.
Shoppers can return unused goods within 7 days of receipt, and can cancel if delivery is more than 15 days late. Your returns and delivery pages should say so.

markets.title: United Arab Emirates
points: Online trade is governed by Federal Decree-Law No. 14 of 2023 on Modern Technology-Based Trade.
You need a commercial licence that includes e-commerce, from your emirate’s Department of Economic Development or your free zone.
Sellers must give accurate product information and a clear digital invoice for every transaction. Standard VAT is 5%.

rules.note: A plain-language summary to help you plan, not legal advice. Check your licence and tax position with the authority in your country before you launch.

sections.heading: Cookies and browser storage
paragraphs: A banner asks for your choice the first time you visit. Google Analytics loads on our pages either way. Until you accept analytics, it’s told not to use cookies, though Google may still receive basic signals without cookies, such as a page having been viewed. We don’t run ads on this site.

Your browser also stores a few small settings, such as your cookie choice and your colour theme. These stay on your device. You can change your cookie choice at any time with the cookie settings button on the page.

answer.heading: What you get for $300
paragraphs: Arabic & RTL gives your website an Arabic version that reads right to left: the layout, navigation, type and spacing are set for Arabic readers, not flipped from the English. It is a fixed price of $300 and takes two to three weeks.

Each Arabic page has its own address and is linked to its English twin, so Google can show the right language to each searcher. This website is built the same way: switch to عربي at the top of any page.
